pp: MPC: BUD / HR / Finance misalignment delays conclusion; MPC revised when operating profit misses target; FTE-by-Brand templates consume disproportionate effort; AZ FORCE missing data at actualisation and new cost centres unavailable; key risk - subjective FTE by Brand and MPC allocations misstate brand-level investment. NMPC: cost template preparation needs copying past cycles and matching actuals; Cost Tool macro errors need the tool owner; repetitive rework; duplicated GL / cost centre lines from previous cycles; key risk - heavy reliance on Cost Tool macros. CAPEX: pending input from the business (primary pain point); delays sometimes come from CBP, who sometimes input directly

rows.act: Power Automate runs the FBL3N extract and saves it to the folder, so data is ready when analysts start. About 30 hours a year per market.

rows.t: Move mapping and transformation into the Power BI semantic model
rows.act: Formula-driven mapping leaves Excel and refreshes on schedule from WD-3 to WD+3. The Excel file was already 80MB by June.

rows.t: Excel connected to the model as the single source of truth
rows.act: Analysts import the prepared P&L dataset into Excel and use pivots or SUMIFS. No second extract for deep dives.

rows.t: Python ad-hoc extraction with manual refresh
rows.act: Analysts can pull a fresh extract and refresh on demand between scheduled runs while the numbers are still moving.

rows.t: Load only the relevant comparator
rows.act: Choose the budget scenario needed in the configuration so redundant comparator data is not carried in the file.

rows.t: Central master-data logic with local cost-centre mapping
rows.act: One central logic for all countries, plus a manual mapping table each country can customise for its own cost centres.

rows.t: Configuration-driven rollout to other countries
rows.act: Malaysia is the pilot. A new market needs only country, local currency and budget scenario set, e.g. Thailand in THB.

rows.t: Finish automating the remaining manual SAP extract
rows.act: In the pilot one SAP extract is still pulled by hand while the other two are saved by an automated workflow.

rows.t: AI first-level variance screening with a moving threshold
rows.act: AI picks the brands, cost centres and GLs above a threshold set to the size of the variance, e.g. 10k or 30–50k. Hackathon output.

rows.t: Customised cost reporting at PO and transaction level
rows.act: Use the same source to show which PO or transaction drives a GL variance. Snowflake is also being explored for this.

rows.t: Fast manual adjustments without a long refresh
rows.act: Late items, e.g. a 100k cost due to post in the afternoon, are added as one line in Excel. Keep this if Excel is ever retired.

rows.t: AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country president
rows.act: Leaders prompt for the main drivers, e.g. sales deterioration versus latest forecast, once the P&L is final.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, market finance: AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country president.

rows.t: Refresh status and failure alert before the day starts
rows.act: Power Automate posts the refresh time and success or failure to the team, so nobody analyses stale data.

rows.t: Automatic tie-out of the model to SAP
rows.act: After each refresh compare model totals with an SAP control total and flag any gap by GL before analysis starts.

rows.t: Daily movement report during WD-3 to WD+3
rows.act: Compare today's refresh with yesterday's and list new postings by GL and cost centre. Shows what moved overnight.

rows.t: Incremental refresh to cut the load time
rows.act: Reload only the open period and keep closed periods static, so the few-minute refresh becomes shorter.

rows.t: Unmapped cost-centre and GL exception list
rows.act: Flag new cost centres or GLs with no mapping at each refresh so they are fixed before they distort the P&L.

rows.t: Structured log for manual adjustments
rows.act: Keep late adjustments in one small table with owner and reason, and clear each line once it posts in SAP.

rows.t: Materiality rule held as a table, not chosen by eye
rows.act: Set the threshold by rule, e.g. % of total variance or Pareto 80%. AI then explains only the items that pass.

rows.t: AI draft commentary with transaction evidence
rows.act: Draft the variance explanation from the top PO and vendor lines behind each flagged item, for analyst approval.

rows.t: Frozen close snapshot for cost reporting
rows.act: Save the WD+3 dataset as a locked version, so cost reporting and later queries use the same numbers.

rows.t: Version control and backup owner for the model
rows.act: Keep configuration and transformation logic under change history with a named backup, so it does not rest on one person.

rows.t: Row-level security before opening to leaders
rows.act: Set access by market and role before CFO or country president use, so each sees only their own P&L.

rows.t: Direct FDH or Snowflake access for budget data
rows.act: Budget data is retrieved by hand once per budget cycle while access is being finalised. Direct access removes the step.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, IT: Direct FDH or Snowflake access for budget data.

rows.t: Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening design
rows.act: FP&A told the hackathon team the tool must serve the P&L while it is still open, not only once it is final.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, hackathon team: Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening design.

rows.t: Deep-dive support for local Embedded Finance
rows.act: Embedded Finance asks for deep dives beyond the global standard dashboards. The model answers them without new extracts.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, Embedded Finance: Deep-dive support for local Embedded Finance.

rows.t: Share the scheduled SAP extraction with other towers
rows.act: The July register already proposes a shared SAP extraction service (FPA-15). Build the job once and reuse it.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, FP&A Ops, R2R, Controlling: Share the scheduled SAP extraction with other towers.

rows.t: Bring known accruals into the pre-close view
rows.act: Late costs are advised informally by Embedded Finance. R2R and P2P accrual lists could feed expected postings in advance.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, R2R, P2P: Bring known accruals into the pre-close view.

rows.t: Shared variance-screening logic with Agent Rhy
rows.act: Both projects pick out drivers above a threshold. Agree one rule set so site and market commentary read the same way.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, FP&A Ops: Shared variance-screening logic with Agent Rhy.

rows.t: Offer the pipeline pattern to other heavy-Excel GL processes
rows.act: Power Automate to semantic model to Excel suits any team working on large GL line-item extracts, e.g. Tax GL Analyzer.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, Tax, Controlling: Offer the pipeline pattern to other heavy-Excel GL processes.

rows.t: Align mapping with the global standard dashboards
rows.act: Use the same hierarchy and definitions as the global dashboards so local deep dives reconcile to reported numbers.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, global reporting owners: Align mapping with the global standard dashboards.

rows.t: Market onboarding pack for rollout
rows.act: Standard checklist per market: configuration, mapping template, access and a parallel-run check against the old file.
rows.xc: Yes — FP&A, market finance: Market onboarding pack for rollout.

High-level process flow

12 processes in 9 stages · Revenue → MPC / CAPEX / NMPC (three streams) → P&L → submission → review deck, then the monthly cycle · bars = activity mix (M manual, S semi-automated, A automated) · click a process to open it on the map
